messages:
sam.devex: Heads-up — running into a weird combo of problems when using async client tool/function calling with structured JSON output. Onboarding a customer sample app and it breaks on long streaming runs.

erin.sdk: ugh, can you paste the minimal repro? framing: are you using the new ToolCall API or the older function-like interface?

sam.devex: new ToolCall API (async). repro snippet below — they expect parsed JSON dicts but sometimes get a raw string chunk mid-stream and then the SDK throws a TypeError on the Pydantic model. Also seeing a 401 retry after ~60s on long runs.

sam.devex: ```py
async with RedwoodAsyncClient(api_key=env.AI_KEY) as c:
    tool_resp = await c.call_tool_async("json_writer", input=my_prompt, structured=True)
    async for msg in tool_resp.stream():
        # expecting dicts
        process(MessageModel.parse_obj(msg))
```

alex.platform: Can you paste the exact error text from the SDK when it hits the raw string? might be the streaming chunk wrapper vs final manifested JSON.

sam.devex: The exception: `TypeError: field 'data' expected dict; got str` — comes from our dataclass coercion in client._parse_stream_chunk. It appears intermittently (15% of streams) when the tool emits a debug line wrapped in backticks.

maria.research: That backtick bit rings a bell — tools sometimes emit human debug logs mid-stream. We should be normalizing tool outputs to JSON when structured=True. The server side currently doesn't enforce content-type for each event.

jon.qa: The 401 is worrying — might be token refresh race. We saw an oauth refresh race in a different module where long-running streams triggered a refresh in a background coroutine and the in-flight connection got 401.

erin.sdk: Two separate bugs then: (A) stream chunk normalization for structured outputs, (B) auth refresh + retry behavior for streaming RPCs. I'll file proper issues but any quick local workaround?

sam.devex: For the customer we patched client._parse_stream_chunk to ignore non_json lines (if structured True) and to buffer until a full JSON object is found. Hacky but reduced failures. For token thing we set an aggressive keep-alive to avoid refresh during runs.

alex.platform: Both sound plausible. I'll open a platform ticket for the auth flow: maybe long-lived streaming websocket uses short-lived token and refresh flow isn't gracefully reauthorized. We can support automatic re-auth on 401 for streaming connections.

erin.sdk: I'll draft a small SDK patch to: 1) treat structured=True as strict (drop non-json events with a debug log + reaction), 2) add typing-safe wrapper that always yields dicts (so MessageModel.parse_obj always gets dicts). Will open PR against repo.

sam.devex: Awesome. Can you also add a sample app in /examples that shows robust consumption with buffering? It's what confused the customer — their quickstart assumed every stream chunk is a JSON object.

erin.sdk: yep. plan: PR #2247 will include tests + example. Tests will include mixed stream with backticks, partial chunks, and an auth 401 simulated mid-stream to assert reconnect/retry semantics.

maria.research: doc note: recommend adding a footnote in the structured output docs explaining that tools may emit non-json diagnostics and SDKs should either drop or surface them as events. Also call out auth behavior for long runs.

jon.qa: I'll add a flaky test in CI that simulates delayed token rotation; want to catch regressions early.

sam.devex: One more ask: can the SDK typing be more explicit in stubs? Right now typechecker flags the generator as AsyncIterator[Union[str, dict]] which forces users to do runtime checks. If SDK guarantees dicts when structured=True we can narrow type to AsyncIterator[dict].

erin.sdk: Good point. I'll update types: AsyncToolStream[T] will be parametric and structured=True => AsyncIterator[dict]. We'll add runtime assertion in the generator to match the typing.

sam.devex: Cool. Thanks team. Customer is fine with the workaround for now but they'd like the example + doc updates before we ship to them.

docbot: Automated note — created issue #1890 (auth/stream-retry) and PR #2247 (sdk/stream-structured-fix).

alex.platform: I'll follow up once we have the platform ticket and a proposed API for stream reauth. :thumbsup:
